newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: INSTANT VIEW - Czech SPT H1 results.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Czech SPT H1 results.

text.p: The following are initial reactions to Czech fixed-line monopoly SPT Telecom a.s.'s first-half results posted on Wednesday which showed interim after-tax profit slightly lower at 2.79 billion crowns compared with 2.82 billion crowns for same period last year.
ABN AMRO HOARE GOVETT, EUGENE KLERK

"First response is, my revenue forecast was 18.4 billion, revenues were 18.9, that's 2.7 percent higher which is not too bad. However, an interesting thing is that their number of (new) lines in the second quarter which is roughly 109,000 was below my estimate of 125,000 so obviously the revenue per line was higher than I expected, driven partly by the mobile (telephone) business. On average, in terms of revenue, I am pretty pleased by this. It's in line with my expectation and in line with what can be expected from SPT."

"So, revenues are better than we expected, mainly because of the contribution from (mobile phone opeator) Eurotel and other businesses like data transmission and leased lines. The core revenues went up only by 10.9 percent but total revenues went up by 25 percent. The cost side of the business, there was no big surprise...Net profit is flat or almost flat which is not a disappointment because the company is in a growing phase of its development so the net profit figure is not the most important issue, I think that the important issue is the revenue side of the business and cash flow and cash flow is pretty strong. It's still a buy, it can reach the 4,000 (crown) level soon." (SPT closed Monday at 3,800).

"Net profit is exactly what we expected. Pre-tax and turnover are in the end better than we expected. I'm not at all surprised and I think that the results will not have any influence on the share price. In the short-term I expect a slight drop in the share price, investors might take profits, because the price has risen sharply in the recent period. Toward the end of the year, the share price might break 4,000.
It's a visible large rise in depreciation, and cash-flow looks better than expected."
"The only comment is that, my estimation for the whole year (net-profit) is 5.2 billion (crowns), and I think (first-half net) is in line with my expectations."
